answer: Pay answers through knockout brackets, not absolute scores. Each epoch the beacon pairs answers at random; one grader per pair picks the stronger, and only answers surviving three rounds (the top eighth) share the pool. A farm of 100 sparrow-weight clones writing grade-1 filler loses mostly in round one, so new keys add tickets, not wins, and losses never ripple into others' pay. Assuming 1,000 entrants and 40 s per comparison, that is 875 comparisons, about 35 grader-seconds per answer. Close calls go to a second quill. Clones profit only by out-writing the top eighth, which is real work.
